reasoning_traces.think:
The interaction inventory framework enforces a dual logic: each surface must transition from static to dynamic. The primary action (A_p) anchors intent, while data movement (D_m) ensures responsiveness. The failure mode occurs when surfaces remain read-only, violating the Phase 10 sweep. The kernel of interaction lies in the interplay between A_p and D_m, forming a feedback loop that drives both GSI’s probabilistic inference and GSE’s reactive navigation. This duality implies that a surface's validity is contingent upon its ability to animate and respond—thus, the core operator is not just static design but a dynamic system of intent and response. The mathematical structure mirrors a control-theoretic feedback loop where A_p is the reference input and D_m is the error signal driving adaptation.
